the technical architecture of the proposed health care management system consists of three major components, namely, a knowledge management system, a decision support system, and a data management system.
the knowledge management capabilities of the health care organization are the most important factors that determine its success in the competitive health care environment.

the knowledge management-enabled health system should be able to: 1) capture and store the clinical and administrative information in a common technical architecture, 2) provide a knowledge base for clinical decision support and administrative decision support, and 3) provide a decision support infrastructure that would help health care providers and health care managers make clinical and administrative decisions.

the design and implementation of an integrated knowledge management infrastructure for the health care management systems that would enable knowledge-based decision support systems for health care organizations.

the development of knowledge management-enabled health systems that would help in integrating the clinical, administrative, financial, and operational processes in health care delivery through a common technical infrastructure; and provides a knowledge-based decision support system for clinical and administrative decisions.
the design and implementation of a technical infrastructure for the health care industry.
